newsitem.title: USA: United Airlines mechanics reject wage offer.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines mechanics reject wage offer.

text.p: Mechanics for United Airlines rejected a wage increase proposal, while ramp, food service, dispatch and other workers that belong to the machinists' union accepted the plan, a union hotline said Thursday.
The recorded message said the mechanics and related employees rejected the wage proposal with 37 percent voting in favour and 63 percent against.

The other workers, who like the mechanics are members of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, accepted the wage package with 67 percent voting for it and 33 percent against it.
The vote tallies were based on preliminary results.
An IAM official said mechanics and related employees at United, a unit of UAL Corp. ,account for about 12,000 to 13,000 of the union's 24,000 members at the airline.
The wage offer for both groups within the IAM was the same, with increases of 3 percent in 1997 and 1998 and 2 percent in 1999 and 2000.

The wage proposal for mechanics will now go to arbitration. Under a clause in the July 1994 employee stock ownership plan, the maximum wage increase that can be awarded in arbitration is 5 percent in 1997 and 1998.
UAL officials were not immediately available for comment.

The wage package stems from a provision in the ESOP agreement. The IAM, along with the Air Line Pilots Association and salaried workers, had swapped wage cuts and work rule changes for a majority stake in UAL.
The flight attendants do not participate in the ESOP.

ALPA is expected to announce its voting results on Jan. 17. An ALPA official said Wednesday that some pilots had campaigned against the wage offer, which also called for pay increases of 3 percent in 1997 and 1998 and 2 percent in 1999 and 2000.
